---
title: "Score patterns with signals"
---

Signals score recent transcript text so a hook fires only when a pattern repeats
hard enough to matter. You pass a `Signals` bundle to a primitive's `signals=`
parameter, set a `threshold`, and let the cumulative score decide. Use this when a
single match is noise but a run of matches is a real behavior, like a retry loop or
a wave of blame-shifting.

For the full signal type list and field defaults, see the
[Conditions Cheatsheet](../reference/conditions.qmd) signals section. To query the
text these signals score, see [Query the transcript](transcript.qmd).

## Match a literal phrase with a regex `Signal`

A `Signal` is a regex worth `weight` points. Every match against a window message
adds `weight` to the running score. Positive weights push toward the threshold;
negative weights suppress false positives.

```python
from captain_hook import Signal

Signal(pattern=r"let me try again", weight=2)
Signal(pattern=r"retry|retrying", weight=1)
Signal(pattern=r"investigating", weight=-3)  # pulls the score back down
```

Set `flags` when you need case-insensitive or multiline matching:

```python
import re
from captain_hook import Signal

Signal(pattern=r"external.*service", weight=2, flags=re.IGNORECASE)
```

## Match meaning with an `NlpSignal`

An `NlpSignal` matches a grammatical relationship instead of a fixed string. It
parses each message with spaCy and checks whether a `Clause` you describe appears in
the dependency tree. This catches paraphrases that a regex would miss.

A `Clause(noun=..., verb=...)` means "this noun is the subject or object of this
verb." So `Clause(noun=Phrase("test"), verb=Phrase("run"))` matches "run the test,"
"the tests ran," and "running a test," because spaCy links `test` to `run` in each.
A `Phrase` holds one or more lemmas, so `Phrase("run", "rerun")` matches either verb.

```python
from captain_hook import NlpSignal, Clause, Phrase

NlpSignal(
    clauses=[
        Clause(noun=Phrase("test"), verb=Phrase("run")),
    ],
    weight=3,
)
```

A `Clause` accepts more than a noun and verb. Add `adj=` to match an adjective on
the noun, set `negated=True` to require a negation, or pass a compound noun phrase on
its own:

```python
from captain_hook import Clause, Phrase

Clause(noun=Phrase.expand("issue"), adj=Phrase("existing", "previous"))
Clause(noun=Phrase.expand("change"), verb=Phrase("cause", "introduce"), negated=True)
```

`Phrase.expand("issue")` pulls in WordNet synonyms of "issue" so the clause matches
"problem," "bug," and other near-synonyms without you listing each one. The bare
`Phrase("existing", "previous")` stays exact.

## Bundle signals with a threshold and window

A `Signals` bundle groups patterns, sets the score `threshold` that triggers the
hook, and bounds the `window` of recent transcript events to score. The window is a
rolling slice of the last N events, so old matches age out as the conversation
moves on.

```python
from captain_hook import Signals, Signal

Signals(
    patterns=[
        Signal(r"retry", weight=2),
        Signal(r"again", weight=1),
        Signal(r"investigating", weight=-3),
    ],
    threshold=3,  # fire once a single message's summed weight reaches 3
    window=10,    # score only the last 10 events
)
```

Each message in the window is scored on its own: every pattern that matches adds
its weight once, and the hook fires when a single message reaches the threshold.
"Let me retry that again" scores 3 and fires; add "investigating" to the same
message and it drops to 0, which holds the hook back.

Set `window="turn"` instead of a count to score the whole current turn. Tool calls
and their results eat window slots, so a fixed window at `Stop` reaches only the
last few tool exchanges. The `"turn"` sentinel reaches back to the prompt that
opened the turn and catches a tell dropped hundreds of events earlier.

You can also pass a bare `list[Signal]` to a primitive. The framework wraps it with
`threshold=1`, so any single match triggers.

## Wire a bundle into nudge

Pass the bundle to `nudge(signals=...)`. The primitive pulls every prose source from
the window — each message's visible text, each thinking block, and the prose fields
of `ReportFindings`, `TaskCreate`/`TaskUpdate`, and `TodoWrite` calls — scores each
entry against every pattern, and warns when one crosses the threshold. It also
deduplicates by content, so the same triggering text doesn't fire the nudge twice in
a row.

```python
import re
from captain_hook import nudge, Signals, Signal

nudge(
    "Stop retrying. Narrow the failing test first, then rerun it once.",
    signals=Signals(
        patterns=[
            Signal(r"let me try again", weight=2, flags=re.IGNORECASE),
            Signal(r"retry|retrying", weight=1, flags=re.IGNORECASE),
            Signal(r"investigating", weight=-3, flags=re.IGNORECASE),
        ],
        threshold=3,
        window=10,
    ),
)
```

When the score crosses 3, the nudge warns and appends a "Triggered by: ..." line
naming the text that set it off, so the agent sees why it fired.

The same `signals=` parameter works on `gate()`, `llm_gate()`, and `llm_nudge()`.
Use `gate()` instead of `nudge()` when crossing the threshold should block the turn
instead of warning.
